answer: Treat each newcomer like a zephyr squeezing through a narrow inlet: the network admits only a fixed number of fresh identities per epoch, picked by lottery among applicants who post a small bond. That bond stays locked like a banked ember and cools back to its owner only after the identity finishes ten epochs of peer-graded work. A sybil farm spinning up thousands of accounts gets a handful through each epoch and ties up capital in every one, so mass identity creation stops paying.
